direction_as_read: Positive for the GutGard extract on dyspepsia and reflux symptoms in two maker-linked trials, and null for older Caved-S ulcer trials; generic deglycyrrhizinated extract at 300 mg has no trial read
summary: Four labels print Gutgard at 75 mg with a digestive purpose, and three print generic deglycyrrhizinated licorice extract at 300 mg. GutGard at 150 mg/day improved functional dyspepsia symptoms (21747893) and reflux quality of life and symptoms (39929150) versus placebo, with primary outcomes named; both are small to mid-sized and maker-linked. Two 1970s Caved-S trials found no ulcer benefit (4584640, 4933135). No generic 300 mg extract trial was found.
question_for_clinician: 21747893 and 39929150 meet rule 2 for GutGard at 150 mg/day, both positive on named primaries. Should the 4 Gutgard labels get credit, given they print 75 mg per row and a maker sponsored or built the trials? Agent recommendation: no credit in this review, with the Gutgard labels flagged as the strongest candidate for a human ruling. The 3 generic 300 mg labels shouldn't inherit GutGard's result, because the trials tested that standardized extract.
